settings.label: Belief-led decisions
settings.help: When on, ASTRA decides whether to own something using only two things: how strongly you believe in its industry, and whether the business itself is still healthy. Price behaviour is then used only to decide how much to buy and when. When off, it falls back to the older method where price and value also vote on whether to own it at all.
settings.impact: Turning this off reverts to the previous scoring method and changes every buy decision. Leave it on unless you are deliberately comparing the two.

settings.label: Buy bar
settings.help: Every candidate gets a score from 0 to 1 that multiplies your belief in its industry by how healthy the business looks. Score this high or above becomes a BUY.
settings.impact: Raise it to buy less often and only the strongest names. Lower it to buy more freely across more of your list.

settings.label: Watchlist bar
settings.help: The same score, but the lower line: at or above this (and below the buy bar) a name is flagged as worth watching rather than bought.
settings.impact: Only affects what shows up as 'watch' on the dashboard. No money moves.

settings.label: Belief weight: very high
settings.help: The score contribution for a stock in an industry you have marked 'very high' belief. This is one of the two halves of the buy decision.
settings.impact: Lowering this can push your strongest-conviction names below the buy bar.

settings.label: Belief weight: high
settings.help: The score contribution for a stock in a 'high' belief industry. Kept below the 'very high' weight so your top convictions always lead.
settings.impact: Raising it toward 1.0 flattens the difference between your best and second-best ideas.

settings.label: Belief weight: medium
settings.help: The score contribution for a 'medium' belief industry.
settings.impact: At 0.6 a medium-belief name needs a near-perfect business to clear the buy bar.

settings.label: Belief weight: low
settings.help: The score contribution for a 'low' belief industry.
settings.impact: At 0.4 these effectively never clear the buy bar on their own.

settings.label: Unknown-business default
settings.help: Some holdings have no company financials to read — funds that hold baskets of stocks, or foreign listings. This is the business-health score they are given instead, so your belief in them carries the decision on its own.
settings.impact: Raising it makes fund-style holdings easier to buy; lowering it sidelines them.

settings.label: Master risk dial
settings.help: The overall volume knob for trade size. Every purchase ASTRA calculates is scaled by this number before any other adjustment.
settings.impact: The single biggest lever here — doubling it roughly doubles every purchase and how fast your cash gets invested.

settings.label: Skip-tiny-trades floor
settings.help: If a calculated purchase would come out smaller than this share of the account, ASTRA skips it rather than placing a trivially small order.
settings.impact: Raise it to cut down on small dribbling buys; too high and weaker signals never trade.

settings.label: New-money cap per run
settings.help: The most of the account ASTRA will commit to brand-new purchases in a single day's run, added across all names.
settings.impact: A brake on going all-in on one dramatic day. Lower spreads entries out over time.

settings.label: Normal jumpiness benchmark
settings.help: ASTRA buys less of a stock that swings wildly day to day and more of a steady one. This is the 'typical daily swing' it compares against — a stock that moves about this much on an average day gets a normal-sized purchase.
settings.impact: Lowering it treats more stocks as jumpy, shrinking most purchases.

settings.label: Most a wild stock is shrunk
settings.help: The floor on that adjustment — even the wildest stock still gets at least this fraction of a normal purchase.
settings.impact: Lower it to be harsher on volatile names.

settings.label: Most a calm stock is boosted
settings.help: The ceiling on that adjustment — the steadiest stock gets at most this many times a normal purchase.
settings.impact: Raise it to lean harder into low-volatility names.

settings.label: Smallest lot (at highs)
settings.help: ASTRA deliberately buys more when a stock is cheap relative to its recent peak and less when it is near its high. This is the multiplier applied when there is no discount at all.
settings.impact: Lower it to almost refuse to buy anything trading at its highs.

settings.label: Biggest lot (deep dip)
settings.help: The other end of that scale: the multiplier when a stock is at a full discount. This is the 'back up the truck' setting.
settings.impact: The main knob for how aggressively you buy falling prices.

settings.label: What counts as fully on sale
settings.help: How far below its highest price of the past year a stock has to fall before ASTRA treats it as maximally discounted and applies the biggest lot multiplier.
settings.impact: Lower it and ordinary dips already trigger maximum buying.

settings.label: Market-crash boost
settings.help: An extra multiplier applied to every purchase when the whole stock market is down, not just your stock. Buying into broad panic rather than a company problem.
settings.impact: At 1.0 the market's own condition stops affecting purchase size entirely.

settings.label: What counts as a full crash
settings.help: How far the overall market has to fall from its high before that boost reaches its maximum.
settings.impact: Lower it and routine market wobbles get treated as crashes.

settings.label: How much rope before selling
settings.help: ASTRA sells a holding if it slides too far from its recent peak. 'Too far' is measured in multiples of that stock's own typical daily move, so a jumpy stock is given more room than a steady one.
settings.impact: Bigger means more patience through normal swings but deeper losses when a decline is real. Smaller sells out quickly and more often.

settings.label: Profit needed before taking some off
settings.help: A winner has to be up at least this much before ASTRA will consider selling part of it. It never sells the whole position for being up.
settings.impact: Lower it to bank profits earlier and more often.

settings.label: How much to sell when trimming
settings.help: When a holding spikes far above its normal range, ASTRA sells this share of it and lets the rest keep running.
settings.impact: Higher banks more cash but leaves less on the table if the run continues.

settings.label: Overheated line
settings.help: One of two conditions for trimming a spike. This is a standard 0–100 momentum gauge — above roughly 70 means a stock has risen unusually fast recently.
settings.impact: Raise it to only trim truly extreme run-ups.

settings.label: How stretched before trimming
settings.help: The second trim condition: how far above its recent average price a stock has stretched, measured in its own typical daily moves.
settings.impact: Higher means only the most extreme spikes get trimmed.

settings.label: Broken business: shrinking sales
settings.help: If a company's sales shrink by more than this compared to a year ago, ASTRA treats the reason for owning it as broken and sells regardless of your belief in the industry. This is the only thing that can override conviction.
settings.impact: The safety valve against holding a genuinely deteriorating company. Loosening it means ASTRA rides declines further down.

settings.label: Broken business: losing money per sale
settings.help: The other break condition: profit left on each dollar of sales falling below this. At 0 it means the company is losing money on every sale it makes.
settings.impact: Raising it above 0 sells companies with thin but positive margins.

settings.label: Real-money trading
settings.help: The master switch for placing real orders in the Robinhood agentic account. Off means ASTRA still decides and paper-trades everything, but places nothing.
settings.impact: Turning this off stops all real trading immediately. Safety switch: if either this or the environment setting says off, trading is off.

settings.label: Daily order cap
settings.help: A hard ceiling on how many orders the Autotrader may place in one day. Purely a brake against a runaway loop, not a strategy setting.
settings.impact: Too low and legitimate buys get silently dropped on busy days.

settings.label: Minimum holding period
settings.help: Trading days a newly bought stock must be held before it can be sold. The account settles trades a day late, so quick round-trips get penalised.
settings.impact: Lower risks account restrictions; higher delays legitimate exits.

settings.label: Cash cushion
settings.help: The share of the Autotrader account that stays as cash and never gets invested. Idle cash is not wasted — the account earns interest on it.
settings.impact: Higher keeps more dry powder for a crash but invests less overall.

settings.label: Spend limit per run
settings.help: The most of its remaining cash the Autotrader will spend in a single day's run. Paces buying out over weeks instead of emptying the account at once.
settings.impact: Higher invests faster and concentrates your entry into fewer days.

settings.label: Smallest worthwhile position
settings.help: The smallest dollar amount the Autotrader will put into any one stock. It buys fewer, properly-sized positions instead of splitting a small budget into many tiny ones. Anything you already own that sits below this gets topped up first — nothing is ever sold to reach it.
settings.impact: Higher means fewer but more meaningful holdings; lower spreads the same money across more names and risks positions too small to matter.

settings.label: How deep a dip is worth texting
settings.help: A stock you already hold is mentioned in the daily note when it is at least this far below its high of the last few months. Shallower pullbacks stay quiet.
settings.impact: Lower texts you about smaller dips; higher only speaks up for real drops.

settings.label: Fallback account size
settings.help: Only used for sizing the paper track when no real account balance has been read yet. Normally your actual Robinhood balance is used instead.
settings.impact: Affects paper trade sizes only when the live balance is unavailable.

settings.label: Extra top-ups per stock
settings.help: After the first purchase of a name, how many additional times ASTRA may add to it while the buy signal persists. Zero means one purchase and no more.
settings.impact: Higher builds bigger positions in names that keep looking good.

settings.label: Wait between top-ups
settings.help: Minimum days between adding to the same stock, so a signal that fires every single day does not buy every single day.
settings.impact: Shorter builds positions faster; longer spreads your average price out.

settings.label: AI judgment layer
settings.help: When on, an AI pass reads your Playbook of strategies and may suggest bounded adjustments — buy a bit more of this, nudge belief slightly. It never makes decisions; every suggestion is capped and re-checked by the rules below.
settings.impact: Turning it off falls back to purely mechanical decisions. Nothing else changes.

settings.label: Most the AI may shrink a buy
settings.help: A hard floor enforced in code on any purchase-size change the AI proposes, no matter what it asks for.
settings.impact: Closer to 1.0 gives the AI less room to shrink positions.

settings.label: Most the AI may grow a buy
settings.help: The matching hard ceiling on any purchase-size increase the AI proposes.
settings.impact: The main limit on how much influence the AI has over trade size.

settings.label: Most the AI may shift belief
settings.help: The AI may nudge a stock's belief score slightly up or down, which can push a borderline name across the buy bar. This caps how far, in either direction.
settings.impact: Set to 0 to forbid the AI from affecting the buy decision at all — it could then only change sizing.

settings.label: Use official filings for small caps
settings.help: Pulls company financials straight from official regulatory filings and layers them over the free market-data feed, which reports poorly on smaller companies.
settings.impact: Turning it off makes business-health scores for small companies less reliable.

settings.label: Max in one stock
settings.help: No single company may exceed this share of the account. Enforced in code on every purchase.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change so the limit stays in version history.

settings.label: Max in one speculative theme
settings.help: No single speculative theme (space names, for example) may exceed this share of the account. Your core technology holdings are exempt.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change.

settings.label: Theme exempt from that cap
settings.help: The one theme allowed to exceed the speculative cap, because it is your core long-term allocation rather than a speculation.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change.

settings.label: Losing-position buy block
settings.help: Once a holding is down this much from what you paid, ASTRA stops buying more of it. Prevents throwing money at a losing position.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change.

settings.label: Buys allowed while down
settings.help: How many additional purchases are allowed on a losing position before the block above kicks in.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change.

settings.label: Emergency stop
settings.help: If the Autotrader's total gain or loss falls this far below the money you have put into it, it stops trading entirely until you step in. Deposits and withdrawals do not trigger it.
settings.impact: Locked. Changing it requires a code change so the circuit breaker stays in version history.

settings.label: Grade my own record
settings.help: When on, at the end of each day ASTRA grades its own track record: how its results compare with simply owning the S&P 500, and whether the companies it picked actually did better than the market. It only reads past history — it never changes a setting and never places a trade.
settings.impact: Turning this off stops the grading and the alerts. Nothing about how ASTRA trades changes either way.

settings.label: Tell me when the grade changes
settings.help: Sends a message only when the conclusion actually changes — for example from 'not enough history yet' to 'doing well, consider adding funds'. A day where nothing changed stays silent.
settings.impact: Off means the grade is still worked out and recorded, just never pushed to your phone.

settings.label: Legacy weight: named holding
settings.help: Used only when belief-led decisions are turned off.
settings.impact: No effect under the current settings.

settings.label: Legacy weight: approved theme
settings.help: Used only when belief-led decisions are turned off.
settings.impact: No effect under the current settings.

settings.label: Weight: hold-only names
settings.help: The score weight for names you have marked hold-only — keep, but do not buy more.
settings.impact: Keeps hold-only names from clearing the buy bar.

settings.label: Legacy buy bar
settings.help: The buy line for the older scoring method. Only used with belief-led decisions off.
settings.impact: No effect under the current settings.

settings.label: Legacy watch bar
settings.help: The watch line for the older scoring method.
settings.impact: No effect under the current settings.

settings.label: Mix: business health
settings.help: How much business health counts in the older combined score. The five mix weights should add up to 1.
settings.impact: Only affects the legacy method and the displayed sub-scores.

settings.label: Mix: cheapness
settings.help: How much price-versus-value counts in the older combined score.
settings.impact: Only affects the legacy method and the displayed sub-scores.

settings.label: Mix: price trend
settings.help: How much the direction of the price counts in the older combined score.
settings.impact: Only affects the legacy method and the displayed sub-scores.

settings.label: Mix: timing
settings.help: How much entry timing counts in the older combined score.
settings.impact: Only affects the legacy method and the displayed sub-scores.

settings.label: Mix: analyst updates
settings.help: How much recent analyst opinion changes count in the older combined score.
settings.impact: Only affects the legacy method and the displayed sub-scores.

settings.label: Sales growth: zero-score point
settings.help: Yearly sales growth at or below this scores 0 for the growth check.
settings.impact: Raising it is stricter about growth.

settings.label: Sales growth: full-score point
settings.help: Yearly sales growth at or above this scores full marks.
settings.impact: Lowering it makes moderate growers look excellent.

settings.label: Profit per sale: zero-score point
settings.help: How much profit is left on each dollar of sales, before overheads. At or below this scores 0.
settings.impact: Raising it penalises low-margin businesses harder.

settings.label: Profit per sale: full-score point
settings.help: Profit per dollar of sales at or above this scores full marks.
settings.impact: Lowering it flatters thinner-margin businesses.

settings.label: Borrowing: healthy level
settings.help: How much a company has borrowed compared to what its owners have put in, as a percentage. At or below this scores full marks.
settings.impact: Lowering it is stricter about debt.

settings.label: Borrowing: danger level
settings.help: Borrowing at or above this level scores 0 on the debt check.
settings.impact: Raising it tolerates far more leveraged companies.

settings.label: Short-term cash: zero-score point
settings.help: Whether a company can cover the bills due within a year from what it can turn into cash within a year. Below 1 means it cannot.
settings.impact: Raising it demands a bigger safety margin.

settings.label: Short-term cash: full-score point
settings.help: At or above this ratio the company scores full marks on covering near-term bills.
settings.impact: Lowering it is more forgiving.

settings.label: Broken-business score ceiling
settings.help: If sales are shrinking badly or the company loses money on every sale, its business-health score is forced no higher than this no matter what else looks good.
settings.impact: Raising it lets clearly deteriorating companies still clear the buy bar.

settings.label: Growth-adjusted price: cheap
settings.help: Price compared to earnings, then adjusted for how fast the company is growing. At or below this counts as cheap.
settings.impact: Only affects the cheapness sub-score.

settings.label: Growth-adjusted price: expensive
settings.help: At or above this the same measure counts as expensive and scores 0.
settings.impact: Only affects the cheapness sub-score.

settings.label: Price vs. expected earnings: cheap
settings.help: How many years of expected profit the share price represents. At or below this counts as cheap.
settings.impact: Only affects the cheapness sub-score.

settings.label: Price vs. expected earnings: expensive
settings.help: At or above this the same measure counts as expensive and scores 0.
settings.impact: Only affects the cheapness sub-score.

settings.label: Cheapness score when data is missing
settings.help: Many holdings have no usable valuation data. They get this middling score rather than being penalised for it.
settings.impact: Moving it away from the middle silently rewards or punishes names with poor data.

settings.label: Trend bonus/penalty size
settings.help: How much being in a clear uptrend adds to the trend score, and being in a downtrend subtracts.
settings.impact: Only affects the trend sub-score and the legacy method.

settings.label: Trend score for a normal dip
settings.help: A shallow dip inside a long-term rise is scored neutrally rather than being punished like a genuine decline.
settings.impact: Raising it treats dips as outright positive.

settings.label: Past-year momentum sensitivity
settings.help: How strongly last year's price performance moves the trend score.
settings.impact: Smaller makes the score react more sharply to modest moves.

settings.label: Distance-from-average sensitivity
settings.help: How strongly the gap between today's price and its recent average moves the trend score.
settings.impact: Smaller makes the score react more sharply.

settings.label: Dip depth limit
settings.help: How far below its long-term average price a stock can sit and still be called a temporary dip rather than a real decline.
settings.impact: Raising it treats deeper falls as harmless dips, which keeps ASTRA buying them.

settings.label: Long-term trend must be rising by
settings.help: The second condition for calling a fall a dip: the long-term average price must still be climbing by at least this much.
settings.impact: Raising it demands a clearly rising trend before dips get bought.

settings.label: Market-link reliability floor
settings.help: Before claiming a stock fell because the whole market fell, ASTRA checks how closely that stock normally tracks the market. Below this the relationship is too weak to trust and the claim is not made.
settings.impact: Lowering it lets weakly-correlated names be treated as market-driven falls.

settings.label: Market drop that counts as panic
settings.help: How far the overall market must fall over a short window to count as a genuine broad selloff rather than ordinary noise.
settings.impact: Closer to 0 fires the crash-buying plays far more often.

settings.label: How widespread the fall must be
settings.help: The share of your tracked stocks that must also be falling, confirming it is a market-wide event and not a few names dragging the average.
settings.impact: Lowering it makes narrow selloffs look like broad panics.

settings.label: New names: minimum sales growth
settings.help: Screening bar applied only to brand-new candidate companies, not to anything you already hold.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: New names: minimum profit per sale
settings.help: Screening bar for new candidates only.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: New names: maximum borrowing
settings.help: Screening bar for new candidates only.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: New names: checks that must pass
settings.help: How many of the five screening checks a new candidate must clear to be considered at all.
settings.impact: Raising it makes new-name discovery much stricter.

settings.label: New names: dip depth wanted
settings.help: How far below its yearly high a new candidate should be to count as a dip opportunity.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: New names: oversold line
settings.help: A 0–100 momentum gauge; below roughly 40 means a stock has fallen unusually hard recently.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: New names: dip signals needed
settings.help: How many of the two dip checks a new candidate must show.
settings.impact: Only affects which new names get suggested.

settings.label: Sweet spot: start
settings.help: How far a stock should have pulled back from its recent peak for the timing to look good, measured in that stock's own typical daily moves. Below this it has barely dipped.
settings.impact: Raising it waits for deeper pullbacks before timing scores well.

settings.label: Sweet spot: end
settings.help: The far edge of that ideal pullback range.
settings.impact: Widening the range makes more moments score as good entries.

settings.label: Too-far-gone point
settings.help: Beyond this the fall is treated as a breakdown rather than a buyable dip, and the timing score drops to 0.
settings.impact: Raising it keeps calling very deep falls buyable.

settings.label: Near-the-average window
settings.help: Buying near a stock's rising recent average price scores well. This is how close counts as near.
settings.impact: Widening it rewards a looser definition of a good entry.

settings.label: Calm-enough line
settings.help: Using the 0–100 momentum gauge: in a rising stock, timing scores full marks at or below this and fades above it.
settings.impact: Raising it lets ASTRA buy stocks that have already run up hard.

settings.label: Too-hot line
settings.help: Where the timing score hits 0 for a rising stock — it has climbed too fast to be a good entry.
settings.impact: Raising it removes the brake on chasing sharp rallies.

settings.label: Capitulation line
settings.help: For a stock in a genuine decline, ASTRA wants real panic before stepping in. Timing scores best around this deeply-sold level.
settings.impact: Raising it accepts shallower falls in a downtrend.

settings.label: Analyst-update sensitivity
settings.help: How many net analyst upgrades or downgrades it takes to move that sub-score to its maximum. This signal is advisory only and never forces a sell.
settings.impact: Minor — the signal carries little weight.

settings.label: Paper: max in one stock
settings.help: The paper track's own ceiling on a single holding, alongside the code-enforced hard limit.
settings.impact: Only affects paper trade sizing.

settings.label: Paper: default purchase size
settings.help: The fallback purchase size used when no explicit size was calculated.
settings.impact: Rarely used — the brain almost always supplies a size.

settings.label: Autotrader is a cash account
settings.help: Cash accounts settle trades a day late and penalise quick round-trips, so extra checks apply before selling. Turn off only if the account type changes.
settings.impact: Turning this off removes those settlement checks.

settings.label: Days of history required
settings.help: How many days where both ASTRA's own value and the S&P 500's value were recorded before it will draw any conclusion at all. Below this it reports 'too early to tell' and says what it is still waiting for.
settings.impact: Lowering it makes ASTRA reach a verdict sooner on thinner evidence, which at these sample sizes mostly means reaching the wrong one.

settings.label: Finished trades required
settings.help: How many positions must have been bought and then fully sold before the grade counts. A position still held has no result yet.
settings.impact: Lowering it lets a handful of lucky or unlucky trades drive the conclusion.

settings.label: Old-enough calls required
settings.help: How many past buy calls must be old enough for their result to be visible.
settings.impact: Lowering it grades ASTRA on calls that have not had time to play out.

settings.label: Different companies required
settings.help: Three hundred results spread over fourteen companies is really fourteen bets, not three hundred. This is the minimum number of different companies that must sit behind those results.
settings.impact: Lowering it lets a couple of names masquerade as a large sample.

settings.label: Different weeks required
settings.help: How many separate weeks the graded calls must be spread across. Calls made in one week all faced the same market and are really one bet on that moment.
settings.impact: Lowering it lets a single good or bad week decide the verdict.

settings.label: Bar for 'doing well'
settings.help: How far ahead of the market ASTRA must be, measured against how bumpy the ride was, before it says the record justifies more money. This is only half the test — the result must also be strong enough that it is unlikely to be luck.
settings.impact: Lowering it makes ASTRA ask for funds on a weaker record.

settings.label: Bar for 'needs attention'
settings.help: The same measure in the other direction: how far behind the market ASTRA must be before it flags that something needs fixing.
settings.impact: Raising it toward zero makes ASTRA raise the alarm more readily.

settings.label: Good pick margin
settings.help: How much better than the S&P 500 the average pick must have done, over the measurement window, to count as genuinely good stock picking.
settings.impact: Lowering it credits ASTRA with skill for beating the market by a hair.

settings.label: Bad pick margin
settings.help: How far behind the S&P 500 the average pick must be before ASTRA concludes the problem is what it chooses to buy, rather than how it buys it. That is the difference between a settings problem and a rethink of your convictions.
settings.impact: Raising it toward zero triggers a strategy rethink on smaller shortfalls.

settings.label: How sure before it speaks
settings.help: ASTRA only calls a result good or bad when the evidence would hold up this often. Higher means it stays quiet longer and is right more often when it does speak up.
settings.impact: Lowering it produces confident-sounding verdicts out of pure noise.

settings.label: Allow for uninvested cash
settings.help: Both tracks deliberately hold some cash, so comparing them against a fully invested S&P 500 makes them look bad in a rising market for a reason that has nothing to do with skill. When on, the comparison is against holding the same proportion in the S&P 500 and the rest in cash.
settings.impact: Turning this off reverts to the raw comparison, which will read as poor execution in almost any rising market.

settings.label: Pick measurement window
settings.help: How long after a buy call ASTRA waits before judging whether it was a good one.
settings.impact: Must match a window ASTRA actually records results for (currently 30 or 60 days); any other value finds no data and the grade stays 'too early'.
